81.body:
tools/generate_level_chunks.py creates deterministic chunks using Pillow. It carves a room/corridor graph on a 48×48 construction grid and expands each cell into a 2×2 tile block. Declared connectors use centered 12-tile openings; undeclared edges stay sealed. Broad ledges support the normal route, while optional movement-gated branches remain off that route. The tool also places and validates authored spike groups. python3 tools/generate_level_chunks.py generate \ --output assets/levels/chunks --prefix generated_chunk --seed 20260825 \ --count 30 --connectors U D L R UD LR UL UR DL DR UDL UDR ULR DLR UDLR
python3 tools/generate_level_chunks.py validate assets/levels/chunks/generated_chunk_*.png
python3 tools/generate_level_chunks.py self-test Use --start-index for another numbered batch, --preview /absolute/path.png for a contact sheet, and --special-branch-rate to change the default 0.75 branch probability. Generation refuses replacement without --overwrite. regenerate <paths...> rebuilds existing 96×96 generated chunks from their stored seeds. Validation checks palette/dimensions, declared openings, sealed edges, the 2×2 geometry invariant, clearances, connected air, substantial wall widths, spike constraints, and mutually reachable core platforms. Its conservative movement model uses a two-tile-tall player, ten-tile upward reach, fourteen-tile horizontal reach, and twenty-four-tile controlled drop. Optional branches must remain excluded from the base traversal graph. These are tool validation bounds, not replacement player-physics tuning. --footprint 3 uses tools/large_level_chunks.py to carve 288×288 cave plans from solid rock, following the room-and-rock proportions of assets/levels/chunks/old_chunks/. Three families provide five winding chambers, four chambers with a looping route, and three chambers with a larger central cavern. Seeded room widths, heights, ceiling contours, side placement, and floor spacing vary their silhouettes. A batch of 45 supplies three plans for every nonempty connector mask: python3 tools/generate_level_chunks.py generate --footprint 3 \ --output assets/levels/chunks --seed 20261001 --count 45 \ --connectors U D L R UD UL UR DL DR LR UDL UDR ULR DLR UDLR
python3 tools/generate_level_chunks.py validate assets/levels/chunks/large_chunk_3x3_*.png
python3 tools/generate_demo_map.py Repeat the large-plan generation command with --overwrite to rebuild the batch. Each PNG records its seed, family, and footprint. Chambers have continuous level floors supported by thick terrain. Irregularity lives in ceilings and side contours; climbs sit beside the chambers and use short, tapered banks attached to the walls. Narrow room mouths preserve those banks, and a horizontal route crossing a shaft has a landing on both sides. All passages are carved before banks are added so intersecting routes preserve each other's footholds. Vertical ports sit beside the end chambers. The main floors remain clear for ground enemies rather than forming diagonal staircases. Cleanup removes corner-only rock contacts and small detached fragments, then fills sealed air pockets. Large-plan validation checks these topology rules, every boundary pixel, the two-tile geometry grid, connected air, and movement both to and from every connector and platform. It also requires at least three encounter floors with 48 uninterrupted tiles of ground and 12 tiles of headroom. Wide-floor traversal samples nearby takeoff and landing positions as well as platform endpoints and midpoints. Room dimensions grow; movement limits and connector openings do not.

Record engine initialization separately from request-to-CPU-ready and request-to-published-frame time. Include adaptation preparation, retained output, and temporary-memory scope. Kernel benchmarks and disk-cached launches do not establish a whole-generation speedup. The selective-biome probe compares full terrain-rule passes with evaluating only the chosen biome and the necessary grass fallbacks, after checking that both choose identical tiles. 83.body: World arrays and the CPU R8 light buffer remain dense. Regional images remove oversized intermediate RGBA surfaces and single-texture dimension limits, but retained assets still grow with the world. Texture residency, eviction, and gameplay streaming are separate work needed for much larger worlds on old laptops. Useful further improvements should remove concrete repeated work: evaluate alternate terrain rules only near changed cells, reuse precomputed candidate offsets where profiling justifies them, and avoid producing empty region buffers. Secret-cover and spike alternatives still build whole-grid logical tile programs even though their raster output is regional. This is a remaining optimization opportunity, not a reason to introduce a general scheduling or dependency framework now. Preserve numerical/visual comparisons and measure the gain before retaining added complexity.

9.body: The Seeker asks questions more than it answers them: The pull of novelty. What draws a Seeker onward, and does the pursuit of new experiences ever end? What would "enough" mean to someone who has already tasted everything ordinary? Expansion and simplicity. One path leads toward more: more knowledge, abilities, power, and possibility. The other leads toward less: humility, service, and letting go. Both should feel genuinely appealing, and neither is presented as obviously right. Recording versus experiencing. Is recording something in the Codex the same as understanding it? Is understanding a creature the same as becoming it? Who benefits. Who gains from the knowledge Theorem gathers, and at what cost? The planet's nature. Is its richness a gift, a call, an accident, or something with no human analogue?
